title: Initial State Memory in Finite Random Brickwork Circuits
summary: We ask under what conditions a finite brickwork circuit of random gates retains local information about the initial state. To answer this question we measure the averaged Frobenius distance between the reduced states obtained by evolving two arbitrary initial states and tracing out a portion of the system. By characterising this distance exactly at all times we find that the information is retained if the environment -- the subsystem traced out -- is smaller than half of the system and washed away otherwise.
